one_line: The Gajapati king of Odisha and the wandering bhakti ascetic whose meeting in Puri unfolded amid war, devotion and debate.

appearance.age_look: Prataparudra looks early 40s, tall and broad-shouldered; Chaitanya looks early 30s, slender with a wiry build.
appearance.face: Prataparudra has an oval face, medium-brown complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache, a small tilaka on his forehead and calm, firm eyes with a composed, duty-bound expression; Chaitanya has a slightly longer face, lighter golden-brown complexion, large expressive eyes, a straight nose, a thin tilaka, and a serene yet intense devotional expression.
appearance.hair: Prataparudra’s hair is black, shoulder-length and wavy, brushed back and mostly hidden under a deep-red Odia royal turban with a subtle gold edge and a single small white feather; Chaitanya’s hair is completely shaven in a clean tonsure with only a faint stubble, leaving his head bare.
appearance.costume: Prataparudra wears a rich ivory-coloured knee-length angarakha-style upper cloth with side-ties and a subtle woven floral pattern, over a deep-indigo dhoti wrapped in the distinctive Odia style with pleats in front and a gold border; over his left shoulder and around his torso is a thick marigold-yellow silk uttariya, and he is adorned modestly with a single medium-width gold necklace, a sacred thread across his chest, simple gold bangles and a couple of finger rings; his feet wear brown leather mojari-style shoes; Chaitanya wears a plain saffron-yellow cotton dhoti wrapped simply and securely, reaching to his ankles with no ornate border, and a matching but slightly lighter saffron upper cloth (uttariya) draped over both shoulders and across his chest, his torso and legs fully covered; he is barefoot, carries no jewellery besides a simple tulasi bead necklace, and his garments are slightly worn, emphasizing renunciation.
appearance.signature: Prataparudra carries a sheathed straight double-edged steel sword with a simple curved crossguard and a plain brown leather scabbard held at his left hip, while Chaitanya carries a small wooden bead mala wrapped around his right wrist, which he often fingers while chanting.

ref_desc: Prataparudra Deva is a medium-brown, early-40s king with shoulder-length wavy black hair under a deep-red Odia turban, wearing an ivory angarakha, deep-indigo dhoti, marigold-yellow silk uttariya and a sheathed steel sword, beside shaven-headed Chaitanya in plain saffron dhoti and uttariya with a bead mala and minimal tulasi necklace, all in indigo, ivory, marigold, saffron and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two linked characters from early 16th-century Odisha: on the left, Prataparudra Deva, an early-40s, tall, broad-shouldered king with an oval, medium-brown face, sharp nose, neatly trimmed moustache, small tilaka and calm, firm eyes; his wavy black hair reaches his shoulders but is mostly covered by a deep-red Odia royal turban with a subtle gold edge and a single small white feather. He wears an ivory-coloured knee-length angarakha-style upper garment with side-ties and a subtle woven floral pattern, a deep-indigo dhoti in Odia wrap with front pleats and a gold border, and a thick marigold-yellow silk uttariya draped from his left shoulder across his torso, with a sacred thread visible beneath. He has a single medium-width gold necklace, simple gold bangles and a couple of rings, and brown leather mojari-style shoes. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon: a straight double-edged steel sword in a plain brown leather scabbard with a simple curved crossguard, held by a cloth belt. On the right, draw Chaitanya, early 30s, slender and wiry, with a slightly longer face, lighter golden-brown complexion, large expressive eyes, straight nose, thin tilaka and a serene yet intense devotional expression; his head is completely shaven with faint stubble and no headwear. He is fully clothed in a plain saffron-yellow cotton dhoti wrapped simply to the ankles and a lighter saffron upper cloth draped over both shoulders and across his chest, covering his torso modestly, barefoot with no ornaments except a simple tulasi bead necklace. His signature prop is a small wooden bead mala wrapped around his right wrist, which he fingers gently. Use a harmonious palette of deep indigo, ivory, marigold yellow, saffron and gold, and show front and three-quarter views to emphasize the fixed face shapes, hairstyles, garments and signature sword and mala without adding any text or labels.
